label: Job-seeking benefit: insured days required before leaving
unit: insured days within the preceding 18 months
appliesTo: Employment insurance subscribers claiming job-seeking benefit
why: Read as six months of employment, which it is not. Insured days count days that were the basis for remuneration plus paid weekly holidays, and exclude unpaid days — so a part-time or irregular schedule can leave someone short after well over six months on the payroll. For a foreign employee there is a second gate that is not in the Employment Insurance Act at all: being lawfully in Korea, on a status permitting work, while unemployed.

history.note: At least 180 insured days in aggregate during the 18 months before leaving, together with the other statutory conditions including the reason for leaving and active job-seeking. Insured days are not calendar days of employment.
